To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose a method to learn local feature descriptor invariance to affine and intensity scale transformation, and that the method can be used to reduce the dimensionality of local feature descriptors by representing them in a binary form.
We propose a novel approach to local feature descriptors that maps high dimensional feature descriptors into the Hamming (0-1) space.

1) we propose a method to improve matching of local features, 2) we demonstrate that our method is effective in practice, and 3) we provide extensive evaluation of our method and comparison with state-of-the-art methods.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed method is able to achieve better results than the SIFT descriptor, while reducing the dimensionality of the descriptors to 64 bits.
the proposed approach can be successfully used to reduce descriptor dimensionality, and to improve matching performance in a variety of scenarios.
the proposed method is a good alternative to SIFT, especially when the size of the dataset and/or the computational complexity are a concern.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Hamming space is a better descriptor space than the Euclidean space.
we have developed a novel descriptor, LDAHash, that has a smaller representation than state of the art, yet achieves state of the art performance in matching and retrieval.
we have proposed an improved local feature matching algorithm which is invariant to affine transformations and intensity scales.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Hamming space representation is a good way of representing local descriptors and that the Hamming metric can be a good way of matching them.
it is possible to obtain high quality feature descriptors that are invariant to affine transformations while being significantly smaller than SIFT.
the Hamming space is a powerful tool in matching and retrieval problems.
